sources.entry: Para - Flexible and modular backend framework/server for object persistence, API development and authentication. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker

summary.one_liner: Para is a scalable, multitenant Java backend server and framework for object persistence, search, caching, and authentication, usable embedded in a JVM app or deployed as a standalone API server.
summary.what_it_does: Para provides a RESTful JSON API for storing and retrieving objects, secured with Amazon's Signature V4 signing and stateless JWT tokens. It is database-agnostic, with DAO plugins named for DynamoDB, Cassandra, MongoDB, and SQL databases, with H2 as the default. Full-text search can use Lucene or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, and objects can be cached locally with Caffeine or distributed with Hazelcast. Each app gets its own table, index, and cache, and features include webhooks with signed payloads, resource permissions, JSR-303 validation, and Dropwizard metrics. The README also mentions an MCP server for AI agents and a Para Web Console admin interface.
use_cases: Backend for a mobile or web application
Multitenant API server shared by several apps
Adding user authentication and access tokens to an app
Embedding a persistence layer in a JVM application
Letting AI agents interact with a backend via MCP
how_to_run: Create an application.conf file in the same directory as the JAR
Install the CLI with: npm install -g para-cli
Run: para-cli setup, then para-cli new-app "myapp" --name "My App"

Or run the Docker image: docker run -ti -p 8080:8080 --rm -v $(pwd)/data:/para/data -v $(pwd)/application.conf:/para/application.conf -e JAVA_OPTS="-Dconfig.file=/para/application.conf" erudikaltd/para:latest_stable
notable: Database-agnostic design with pluggable DAO, search, cache, queue, file store, and emailer implementations
Client-side admin console: the secret key stays in the browser and a JWT is generated locally for each request
Per-app multitenancy, with each app getting its own table, index, and cache
Can run embedded in a JVM application or as a standalone multitenant API server
Optional native image build via Maven profile
caveats: The README describes the Elasticsearch v5 integration as deprecated.
Native images are platform-dependent and must be built per architecture.
Hosted managed service and premium support are offered by Erudika at paraio.com, and the README lists paid tiers there.
The README says the :latest Docker tag can be broken or unstable, so release tags are recommended.
